newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up, with the earliest-maturing three-day contract hitting a record high due to continued new domestic A shares issues, traders said.
The annual rate for the contract, the most active one today, soared to 28 precent from 15.26 percent on Tuesday.
"The contract hit a new high due to active buying from big institutions for new share issues," a trader said. There are six new share issues and listings in Shanghai this week.
Turnover fell rose sharply to 13.03 million lots from 6.06 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said most of the repo rates were likely to go down on Thursday when speculative trading on new shares decreases.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended down on Wednesday and institutions seemed to be cautious before the issue of new seven-year treasury bills early next month.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 123.47 yuan from 123.55 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 4.93 million lots from 2.73 million.
Traders expect the contracts to move in a narrow range in the short term. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
